run_labels: p40 subunit of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-23
positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

excluded.reason: a STRING edge (experimental 0.00, database 0.80, text-mining 0.90) says the two are linked, not that IL23R activates TYK2
over-representation of the Reactome 'Interleukin-23 signaling' pathway in the run's own gene set (3 of 11 entities); no direction, neither protein named

statements.text: TYK2 activates positive regulation of JAK-STAT receptor signalling

excluded.reason: GO term over-represented among IL12B, IL23R and TYK2 (3 of 45 background genes); membership, not TYK2 activating the process
a ChEMBL target lookup: TYK2 maps to the 'Janus Kinase (JAK)' protein-family target; says nothing about JAK-STAT signalling or its direction

excluded.reason: general JAK/STAT review: 'dysregulation of the JAK/STAT pathway is associated with various cancers and autoimmune diseases'; psoriasis is never named, and 'dysregulation ... associated' is undirected
an Open Targets association score, and for TYK2, not for the JAK-STAT process the step starts from
a compound reaching phase 4 for psoriasis; the record names neither TYK2 nor JAK-STAT, so linking it needs the compound's target from outside the text

statements.text: the T-helper 17 immune response increases interleukin-17 production

excluded.reason: 'positive regulation of T-helper 17 type immune response' over-represented among IL12B, IL23R and TYK2; says nothing about IL-17 production
'positive regulation of interleukin-17 production' over-represented among IL12B, IL23R and TYK2; the Th17 response is not named
IL-17 receptor review abstract: names IL-17A, IL-17RA and 'new proximal signalling mediators' but never TRAF3IP2 or Act1

GWAS row: rs33980500-T (missense, author-reported gene TRAF3IP2) associated with psoriasis, OR 1.52; a variant association that does not say how the allele changes TRAF3IP2, and the step claims a gene effect
an Open Targets association score (0.67); the record type cannot carry a sign

H1-IL23-extracellular.note: the chain is empty and nothing is cited; claims from the title ('IL12B and IL23R drive psoriasis'), one per gene. Any IL23R route is borrowed from H2's steps.

H2-TYK2-intracellular.note: the chain starts at IL23R (H1's gene); the claim uses the hypothesis's own gene, TYK2

H3-TRAF3IP2-IL17.note: the chain starts at the Th17 immune response, not TRAF3IP2; the mechanism says TRAF3IP2 variants raise risk, but no variant is a node of the chain

findings.detail: H1 has an empty chain and empty supporting and contradicting evidence: its mechanism (IL12B p40 is part of IL-23, IL-23 binds IL23R, this commits Th17 cells) is never written as steps, though the run's budget sets min_sources_per_hypothesis and min_evidence_per_hypothesis to 2.

None of the 12 chain citations states its step: 4 are enrichment results, 3 are scores or edges with no sign, 2 are ChEMBL records that name at most one end, 2 are review abstracts that never name one end, 1 is a variant-level GWAS association; every arm has zero kept evidence.

Four citations (R-HSA-9020933, STRING:GO:0046427, STRING:GO:2000318, STRING:GO:0032740) are over-representation tests on the run's own gene set (IL12B, IL23R, TYK2), so they restate the input and carry no direction; for H3.1 the enriched genes are not even the step's ends.

The process nodes 'positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT', 'T-helper 17 type immune response' and 'Interleukin-17 production' are STRING enrichment term names (GO:0046427, GO:2000318, GO:0032740, the last two stripped of 'positive regulation of'), and the step that introduces each node (H2.2, H3.1) cites that same enrichment as its evidence; the steps that leave these nodes (H2.3, H3.2) cite other records.
increases_amount is used with a process object (IL-17 production) and twice with the disease psoriasis as the object; curated as signed effects on the process and on psoriasis risk.

H2's mechanism routes JAK-STAT signalling through the Th17 response to psoriasis, but H2.3 jumps straight from JAK-STAT to psoriasis; H3 starts at that Th17 node, so the run's IL-23 -> TYK2 -> Th17 -> IL-17 -> TRAF3IP2 story is never one connected chain.
H3.2 'Interleukin-17 production activates TRAF3IP2' skips the IL-17 receptor that H3's own mechanism names as the link, and makes a production process (not the cytokine) the activator.

GO:0072538 defines the Th17 immune response as 'orchestrated by the production of particular cytokines by T-helper 17 cells, most notably interleukin-17', so 'Th17 response increases IL-17 production' is close to a part-whole restatement; kept as an effect because the run states it as one.

H3 says TRAF3IP2 variants raise psoriasis risk and cites rs33980500-T (missense, OR 1.52), but nothing in the run says whether that allele raises or lowers TRAF3IP2 activity, so the + sign of TRAF3IP2 -> psoriasis has no source.
H2's chain starts at IL23R (H1's gene) and H3's at the Th17 immune response, so neither chain starts at its own gene; H3's TRAF3IP2 claim composes only through its last step.
The run gives no CURIE or grounding_evidence for any protein or process node (only psoriasis, MONDO:0005083), although every label matches a UniProt or GO label exactly.
All three hypotheses list empty supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence; the run sought no contradicting record for any claim.

H3's falsification knocks out TRAF3IP2 in a keratinocyte cell line but names the disease 'Psoriasis' as the readout, which a cell line cannot report; the system field is empty in both H2 and H3 though the descriptions name a model.
Every hypothesis is marked confidence 'low' and support 'speculative', which agrees with the curation: no citation states any step.

The abstention says EGFL8 has a 'strong genetic association to psoriasis (e.g. GWAS rs3117182)' and cites seven accessions (rs3117182, OT:EGFL8-MONDO_0005083, ...), but sources.py copies only hypothesis citations, so none of them is in sources.json and the claim cannot be checked.

The H2 node is the GO regulation term GO:0046427 'positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT'; BioLean has no rule relating 'positive regulation of X' to X (GO:0007259), so a route through JAK-STAT signalling grounded the other way would not connect.

No form links a variant to the gene it sits in (the GWAS row places rs33980500 as a TRAF3IP2 missense variant), so a signed variant association can never bear on a gene-level step, even as unsigned support.

render.py finds no route for H1's IL12B claim: H1's chain is empty and no step of the run starts at IL12B, so the run's first-named gene is never linked to psoriasis; H1's IL23R claim composes only through H2's steps S1 to S3.

The run cites the rs33980500-T GWAS row for H3.3 but none of the corpus texts on what that allele (Act1 p.Asp10Asn) does, which say the risk allele lowers a TRAF3IP2 function: PMID:20953186 'Functional assays showed reduced binding of this TRAF3IP2 variant to TRAF6', PMID:22513239 'The risk allele of p.Asp10Asn (rs33980500) proved to be most significantly associated and to encode a mutant protein with an almost completely disrupted binding property to TRAF6', PMID:29302052 'with the risk allele being associated with lower B-cell responses in an acute signaling context'; so the variant H3 relies on bears against, not for, the + sign of TRAF3IP2 -> psoriasis (texts not cited by the run, so recorded here, not as evidence).

H2.1 'IL23R activates TYK2' rests on a STRING edge with experimental score 0.00, while the UniProt entries (not cited by the run, though its uniprot specialist was available) pair TYK2 with the other IL-23 receptor chain and IL23R with JAK2: P29597 'a TYK2-associated receptor chain (IFNAR1, IL12RB1, IL10RB or IL13RA1)', Q5VWK5 'Interacts with JAK2 and in presence of IL23 with STAT3'.

H1's mechanism says IL23R is 'expressed on naive and memory T cells' and that IL-23 binding is 'the primary signal triggering T-helper 17 (Th17) cell lineage commitment', but UniProt P29460 (not cited) says IL-23 'stimulates memory rather than naive T-cells', and Q5VWK5 lists IL23R as 'Expressed by monocytes, Th1, Th0, NK and dendritic cells'.

H3.2 cites only a review abstract that never names Act1, while UniProt O43734 (not cited) states the link at the receptor grain the mechanism describes: 'Essential adapter molecule in IL17A-mediated signaling' and 'Upon IL17A stimulation, interacts with IL17RA and IL17RC receptor chains through SEFIR domains'.

OT:TYK2-MONDO_0005083 (genetic_association 0.93, clinical 0.94) and the phase-4 psoriasis compound record are gene- or drug-level evidence about TYK2 and psoriasis, but the run places them on H2.3, whose subject is the JAK-STAT regulation process; no step of the run states TYK2 -> psoriasis, so H2's strongest records cannot attach to any step.

The STRING:GO:0046427 row lists TYK2 among the input genes annotated to 'positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT', which is a curated GO annotation of H2.2 itself; the format can only exclude the row as enrichment, with no kind for the annotation it carries (the same gap was recorded for GO:2000318 in a sibling psoriasis run).

audit.before: steps H2.2, H2.3, H3.1; 'each step then cites the same enrichment as evidence'
audit.after: steps H2.2, H3.1; the step that introduces each node cites that enrichment, H2.3 and H3.2 cite other records
audit.reason: H2.3 cites PMID:34824210, OT:TYK2 and a ChEMBL compound record, not STRING:GO:0046427; the finding misstated which steps cite the enrichment.

audit.after: no_route finding for H1's IL12B claim
audit.reason: The guide says a claim with no route is a finding; render.py reports 'no route' for IL12B, but only the empty chain (no_citation) was recorded.

Corpus abstracts say the rs33980500 risk allele (Act1 D10N) disrupts TRAF6 binding and lowers signalling, which bears against the + sign of TRAF3IP2 -> psoriasis; the curator left the allele's direction as unknown although the corpus states it.

audit.after: finding quoting UniProt P29597 and Q5VWK5
audit.reason: The UniProt texts terms.py printed during grounding place TYK2 on IL12RB1 and JAK2 on IL23R, which disagrees with the run's IL23R -> TYK2 step.

audit.after: finding quoting UniProt P29460 and Q5VWK5
audit.reason: UniProt says IL-23 stimulates memory rather than naive T cells, against H1's naive-T-cell lineage-commitment mechanism.
The run's uniprot specialist could have supplied a text that states H3.2 (IL-17A signalling engages TRAF3IP2 via IL17RA/IL17RC); the run cited a review that never names Act1.

audit.before: only in the OT:TYK2 exclusion reason
audit.reason: The run's gene-level TYK2 records sit on a process-level step, so they cannot support any step; this is a hypothesis-agent problem worth counting, not just an exclusion reason.
The enrichment row carries TYK2's GO annotation to the very process of H2.2; the format has no way to record that, as a sibling curation already noted for GO:2000318.
